title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: the continuous batcher scheduler was showing unfair queueing behavior under mixed-latency workloads (short text completions vs long-context streaming requests). This caused starvation for low-throughput classes and spiky tail latency for latency-sensitive customers. This PR introduces scheduler tuning and a small refactor to prevent starvation, enforce queueing fairness across priority classes, and add conservative per-request timeouts to avoid unbounded KV-cache holds.

Summary of changes: implement a weighted round-robin queue drain with aging bonuses, introduce per-class queue length soft-limits and exponential backoff for long-waiting entries, add a per-request maximum KV-cache hold timer that forces a graceful fallback path (requeue to a fallback pool) on timeout, expose runtime knobs for fairness weights and starvation thresholds, and add end-to-end benchmarks and unit tests validating fairness and timeout behavior.

Technical details: 1) Scheduler refactor: split scheduling into a lightweight queueing layer (QueueManager) and a drain policy (DrainPolicy). QueueManager tracks per-class statistics (enqueue_time, attempts) and exposes an API that does not block on KV cache; DrainPolicy implements weighted round-robin with aging_bonus that increments for entries waiting > starvation_threshold_ms. 2) Starvation prevention: entries that exceed starvation_threshold_ms get an aging_bonus which bumps their effective weight; after crossing max_starvation_ms they are moved to a best-effort lane that guarantees dispatch within a bounded window. 3) Timeouts and KV-cache holds: when a request acquires a KV-cache slot, a background timer is started (kv_hold_timeout_ms). If timer fires before the request produces output, the runtime triggers a best-effort fallback where the request is re-enqueued to a cacheless path and metrics are emitted. 4) Config knobs: fairness_weights (per-class), starvation_threshold_ms, max_starvation_ms, kv_hold_timeout_ms, best_effort_lane_ratio. 5) Observability: emit new metrics (scheduler.enqueue_time_ms, scheduler.aging_bonus, scheduler.requeued_to_fallback, kv.kv_hold_timeout_count) and add tracing spans in QueueManager and DrainPolicy.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks show 12-18% median latency improvement for mixed workloads and 30-45% reduction in 99.9th percentile starvation events for low-throughput classes in our internal perf-lab. End-to-end perf runs included both GPU-backed and CPU-only model variants.

Testing: unit tests for QueueManager/DrainPolicy, integration tests in perf-canary harness simulating mixed bursty workloads, and a canary rollout on dedicated pools with traffic shaping for 24h. Added Linear test plan under ENG-1123.

Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pools (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if scheduler.requeued_to_fallback or kv.kv_hold_timeout_count increases by >20% vs baseline. Feature flags are behind runtime config in runtime.yaml and accessible via console for Dedicated.

Risk and mitigation: risk of misconfiguration causing excessive requeues; mitigated by conservative defaults that match current behavior (aging_bonus starts at 0, starvation_threshold_ms defaults to 200ms). Added feature flag and runtime metrics to alert on behavioral regressions.

Related: builds on prior continuous-batcher tuning PRs (see recent series pr-41213, pr-42876, pr-47603) and aligns with KV cache work ENG-1189.

How to revert: revert the single merge commit (squash) or flip the runtime feature flag to restore previous scheduler path.

Notes: description is intentionally compact — see code comments and unit tests for exact algorithm and formulas.

review_comments: Michael Chen (reviewer): The aging bonus logic looks reasonable but can you clarify why we use exponential backoff on attempts instead of linear? Also please add a comment linking to the perf graphs used to pick defaults.

Ava Martinez (author): Reply: exponential backoff reduces oscillation under heavy contention; added a comment and linked perf graphs in the code and the PR description. Kept conservative default coefficients as discussed.

Priya Singh (reviewer): Can we ensure the kv_hold_timeout doesn't fire prematurely for long-token streaming requests? Suggest adding a per-route override and a telemetry tag so we can correlate with streaming endpoints.

Ava Martinez (author): Reply: added per-route override capability and attached telemetry tag kv_hold_timeout_route. Also added tests to ensure streaming routes can opt-out by setting kv_hold_timeout_ms=0.
Luca Rossi (approver): Approving after small nits fixed (typo in metric name). Confirmed canary metrics look healthy at 50%.
release_notes: Improved continuous batcher scheduler fairness and starvation prevention with new runtime knobs and KV-cache timeout fallback. Reduces starvation events for low-throughput classes and improves mixed-workload tail latency. Defaults are conservative; no breaking behavior expected.
additional_notes: Canary rollout observed 35% reduction in 99.9th percentile starvation incidents for small requests
Operational knobs are exposed in runtime.yaml and Console; recommend enabling for Dedicated first
